text.p: The Croatian government on Tuesday presented an amended 1997 budget proposal, increasing expenditure for welfare programmes and wages to help the worst-off citizens, state radio said on Tuesday.
Quoting a government statement, the radio also said the government's spending on office perks and official cars would be trimmed.
The original 39.4 billion kuna ($7.22 billion) budget proposal included an increase of about 10 percent from this year's spending, designed to spur economic recovery and boost welfare programmes.
The deficit of some 2.8 billion kuna would be financed by domestic and foreign borrowing.
The amended draft foresees an increase in wages for public sector workers and higher payouts for social programmes aimed to help war invalids.
It will also allow more money for road building and for loans to aid demobilised soldiers who set up businesses, the radio said.

Croatian Parliament last month backed the budget draft despite strong criticism from opposition members who described it as too "bureaucratic" and "centralised" and slammed the government's spending as excessive.
The budget is expected to be approved this month. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
